title: Latency & Stability Scorecard and Customer Acceptance Protocol for Dedicated Throughput
creator: Anika Rao
description: Build a repeatable, lightweight validation and handoff protocol that measures not only sustained throughput but also latency stability under realistic tenant mixes for Dedicated capacity customers. Deliverables: 1) a quantile-driven scorecard (latency/stability/throughput/cost), 2) a runnable harness template for customer acceptance runs, and 3) a checklist + gating rules for signoff and rollout to Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Scorecard computes p50/p90/p99/p999 latencies and a stability index (0-100) for a supplied replay or synthetic workload
Harness reproduces customer-shaped arrival patterns (burst, ramp, steady-state) and can run in CI or on-customer staging clusters
Gating rules: pass if throughput >= committed TPS ±5% for 30m sustained and p99 latency <= committed SLO; otherwise fail and capture KV cache, batching stats, and kernel selection snapshot
Customer acceptance runbook and checklist published to Confluence and linked in onboarding flow
Two example customer runs completed with cross-functional signoff (SRE, Product, Solutions)
runbook_steps: 1) Prepare: collect customer contract (TPS, model, max_seq_len), sample corpus, and tenant-count estimate
2) Provision: allocate a staging Dedicated fleet matching the customer’s SKU, enable telemetry (tracing, token-level cost, kernel profiles)
3) Configure harness: choose replay vs synthetic profile; set ramp (5m), sustain (30m), burst window (2m) and failure injection knobs
4) Dry run: run 5m smoke to validate request shaping, authentication, and telemetry export paths
5) Full run: execute ramp->sustain->bursts while collecting latencies, queue times, batching histograms, KV cache hit-rates, and autoscaler events
6) Scorecard generation: compute quantiles, stability index, and cost-per-1k-tokens; produce a single-page PDF report
7) Review: engineering and SRE review traces and kernel logs; if failing, capture mitigations and rerun
8) Customer signoff: Solutions Engineering walks customer through report, demonstrates reproducibility, and records approval
scoring_notes: Stability index = 100 - (weighted variance score of p99 over sliding windows) - (burst_reaction_penalty) - (cache-miss penalty). We weight recent windows higher. Full formula documented in Confluence link.

risks_and_open_decisions: How strict should the cost deviation tolerance be when customers have bursty usage? Current proposal: +/-10% cost variance tolerated for first 90 days.

Decision: whether to require 100% telemetry sampling for all acceptance runs (SRE pushed back due to storage). Proposal: enable 100% only for short acceptance windows and archive logs to lower-cost object store.

Risk: Autoscaler interactions may mask kernel-level regressions if we allow scaling during the steady-state window. Temporary mitigation: annotate scale events and fail if p99 increases > 25% within 60s of a scale event.
